text:
Lina: Hi everyone, excited to join! Quick environment puzzle on macOS Ventura (M1) while following the new-hire bootstrap: after `brew install asdf` and adding asdf to my `.zprofile`, `asdf install python 3.11.4` fails with `ssl module missing` and `ensurepip` errors. I tried `brew install openssl readline xz` and exporting flags, but still seeing `cannot find -lssl` during link stage. Anyone seen this exact symptom?

Omar: welcome Lina! :wave: A couple quick checks: is Homebrew installed under `/opt/homebrew` and is that early in your PATH? `echo $PATH` and `which openssl` help. Also check `brew list --versions openssl@1.1 openssl` to see which formulae are present.

Lina: `which openssl` -> `/opt/homebrew/bin/openssl` and `brew list --versions` shows `openssl@3 3.2.0` but not `openssl@1.1`. I remember some projects requiring 1.1 for build compatibility.

Omar: try `brew install openssl@1.1` and then export the build flags before running asdf install:```bash
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig"
asdf install python 3.11.4
```
Also if you have `PYTHON_CONFIGURE_OPTS` set in your dotfiles it can change artifacts (sometimes removes ensurepip).

Lina: did that, build succeeded but `python -m ensurepip` failed at runtime with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ensurepip'`. Checking `python -V` and `which pip` shows `pip` missing from the shim.

Omar: The asdf python plugin uses python-build; ensure you don't have system-level `python` shim collisions. After install run `asdf reshim` and check `python -m ensurepip --default-pip`. If `ensurepip` was excluded during build, you can bootstrap pip with `curl -sS https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py | python -` as a last resort. But better to rebuild without flags that disable ensurepip.

Lina: Rebuilt after unsetting `PYTHON_CONFIGURE_OPTS` and `pip` is present. Now a smaller annoyance: my dotfiles symlink `~/.zprofile` -> `~/dotfiles/shell/.zprofile` sets `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"`, but when I open iTerm I still see the old system python at `/usr/bin/python`. Any ideas?

Omar: login vs interactive shells can differ. On mac zsh: `.zprofile` is for login shells and `.zshrc` for interactive ones. If iTerm opens a non-login interactive shell, ensure you source asdf init in both or put the PATH prep in `.zshenv` which runs for all shells. Example in `.zshenv`: `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"; . "$HOME/.asdf/libexec/asdf.sh"`

Lina: Ah, I had it only in `.zprofile`. Moved to `.zshenv` and now `which python` points to `~/.asdf/shims/python`. Thanks! Last two Qs: 1) pre-commit hooks fail with `command not found: flake8` despite flake8 in pyproject toml and poetry installed. 2) who owns the `dotfiles` repo for a quick sanity review?

Omar: For pre-commit + asdf/poetry: pre-commit runs hooks in the repo environment. If hooks are configured to use `system` or `python` interpreters, ensure your `pre-commit` is installed in the right python environment, and that the hook uses `language: python` so pre-commit creates isolated venvs. Check `.pre-commit-config.yaml` entries. If you rely on a workspace venv (poetry), you can set `PRE_COMMIT_HOME` to cache and `poetry run pre-commit install`.

Lina: `.pre-commit-config.yaml` does `repo: local` with `entry: flake8` and `language: system` (oops). Changing to `language: python` and letting pre-commit manage venvs fixed the missing flake8. I also added `poetry run pre-commit run --all-files` to my CI step.

Lina: About dotfiles review: I opened a small PR at https://github.com/redwood-onboarding/dotfiles/pulls/12 tagging `@devex` for review.

Security: Quick PSA: when you add files like `SETUP.md` to dotfiles, avoid checking in any `env.local` or files that contain tokens/credentials. Use `.envrc` with direnv and ensure `.envrc` loads secrets from 1Password rather than plaintext. If you need a sample file, use `SETUP.example` not actual secrets.

Lina: Thanks Security, I scrubbed my PR and replaced an accidentally committed `local.env` with `SETUP.example`. Also ran `git filter-repo` per the incident guide. All good now.

Omar: fantastic. One last DevEx tip: commit an `asdf/.tool-versions` in your dotfiles to pin runtimes (helps CI reproducibility). Welcome aboard Lina!

Devex Bot: Congrats on getting past bootstrap issues! DevEx checklist: `brew`, `asdf`, `direnv`, `1password-cli`, `docker` (if needed), and `commit .tool-versions`. Docs: https://redwood.ai/devex/bootstrap. If you want in-person pairing for dotfiles, DM `@omar`.
